clue.text: Setter ordered horse for homeless child

indicators.note: ordered means the letters of the word setter are put into a new arrangement

parts.note: an Arab is a breed of horse

explanation.surface: A crossword compiler appears to be sending a horse off to look after a child with no home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like the crossword's own author, but here it is just six letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Street arab is a dated term for a destitute child living rough in city streets.

clue.text: Murder an unorthodox sort of bowling

indicators.note: unorthodox signals that the letters of murder an are to be arranged in an unconventional order

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator complains that a bowler's odd delivery style is criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: Underarm bowling, delivered with the hand below shoulder height, is a style of bowling in cricket and other games.

clue.text: Prisoner might get this job as secretary?

parts.note: a PA, personal assistant, is a secretary
a role is a job or position

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a convict might be given office work as a secretary.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces appear in reverse order in the clue: a job (ROLE) as a secretary (PA) reads as a PA role.
explanation.definitionFit: Early conditional release from jail is something an inmate may be granted for good behaviour.

clue.text: Country base that is without a castle

parts.note: e is the base of natural logarithms in mathematics

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the castle letter sits inside the that-is abbreviation

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
R is the chess notation for a rook, also called a castle

explanation.surface: A nation is described as a military base with no fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside here. R for castle comes from chess, where the rook is also called a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish name for the Republic of Ireland, a nation state.

clue.text: Bad press? No setter's inclined to answer

indicators.note: bad signals the letters of press no are spoilt into another order

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as I, so setter's is I've, I have

explanation.surface: A compiler, stung by negative newspaper coverage, is keen to reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter's' stands for 'setter has', I'VE, since the setter is 'I'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone quick to react or reply readily is described this way.

clue.text: Male with stamina rigged part of boat

indicators.note: rigged means arranged dishonestly, so the letters of stamina are shuffled

explanation.surface: A strong man has fitted out a sailing vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rigged' fits the nautical picture, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal mast of a sailing ship is one component of the vessel.

clue.text: Go for tips from Clark Kent after a time looking in the mirror

indicators.note: after places the tips of the two names behind the mirrored pair

parts.words: a time looking in the mirror
parts.note: a gives A and time gives T; AT gazing into a mirror is shown with its reflection TA beside it, making a four-letter palindrome

indicators.note: tips from takes the leading letters of the two names

explanation.surface: Superman's alter ego, after a while checking himself in a mirror, decides to charge in.
explanation.walkthrough: AT seen in a mirror becomes AT plus its reflection TA. Clark Kent is Superman's everyday identity.
explanation.definitionFit: To go for someone is an idiom for assaulting or setting upon them.

clue.text: A villain finally turning up on the fifth dimension's fourth hub

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards, that is backwards
finally takes the last letter of villain

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five, standing for fifth

indicators.note: fourth picks the fourth letter of the word dimension

explanation.surface: A sci-fi baddie finally appears in the centre of a fourth-dimensional world.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the later pieces below the reversed A and N.
explanation.definitionFit: The central body of a church, or the hub of a wheel, are both senses of this word.

clue.text: Around time a silent 'a' affected 13

indicators.note: around means the shuffled letters are placed around the time letter
affected means altered, so the letters of a silent a are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grammar note about a mute letter that somehow teases.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer to 13 across, TEASE.
explanation.definitionFit: To tantalise is to torment someone by showing them something they cannot have, which is to tease them.

clue.text: Component of fast racing car

indicators.note: Component of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A part from a speedy competition car is being described.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vauxhall Astra is a model of motor car sold in Britain.

clue.text: Setter observed by hearing or sight

indicators.note: by hearing says the phrase is to be judged by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: the setter is I, and observed is saw, giving I saw

explanation.surface: A compiler claims to have noticed something by ear or by eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sight' looks like vision, but it is the definition in its sense of an ugly thing; 'or' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sight can mean something ugly to look at, as in 'you look a sight', an unsightly object.

clue.text: George Eliot was one in a million into pasta

indicators.note: into says the pieces are put inside the pasta

parts.note: penne is a tube-shaped pasta

explanation.surface: A tribute calling a famous Victorian novelist exceptional, with an odd addition about pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: George Eliot was the name Mary Ann Evans wrote under.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary Ann Evans published as George Eliot, an assumed authorial name.

clue.text: Meal with ends of spare rib

parts.note: tea is an evening meal in British usage

indicators.note: ends of takes the first and last letters of spare

explanation.surface: A dinner served with the tips of spare ribs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rib' looks like part of the meal but is a verb meaning to mock gently. TEA is the British name for an early evening meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To rib someone is to make fun of them playfully, to taunt them good-naturedly.

clue.text: One searching thoroughly gets answer in TV series? Not initially

indicators.note: not initially says the first letter of the assembled word is dropped
in places the abbreviation inside the series title

parts.note: Cracker was a British TV crime drama series starring Robbie Coltrane

explanation.surface: A detective combing a crime scene features in a television drama.
explanation.walkthrough: Cracker was a 1990s British TV drama about a criminal psychologist; 'Not initially' removes its C.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransack is to search a place thoroughly, often roughly, so the noun is someone who does so.

clue.text: Gem of a girl, unknown to drink two pints

parts.note: Rose is a girl's name
a quart is a measure of two pints
Z is one of the letters used for an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: A lovely young woman is unaware someone is downing a large quantity of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gem of a girl' reads as praise, but 'Gem' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose quartz is a pink variety of the mineral used as a semi-precious stone.

clue.text: Raw duck's foot, cooked with almond in a haphazard series of steps

indicators.note: cooked means prepared or fiddled, so the letters are rearranged
foot, in a down clue, means the bottom or last letter of duck's

explanation.surface: A recipe in which uncooked duck feet are prepared with nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: A random walk is a mathematical path where each step is in a chance direction.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics and physics, a path made of successive random steps is known by this name.

clue.text: Golfer lists family members following behind imp and trickster

indicators.note: following places the remaining pieces after the word for behind

parts.note: a rump is the behind or bottom
Ernie Els is a South African golfer
a ship lists or tilts when it leans
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: A golfer leans over and his relatives trail along behind him.
explanation.walkthrough: The fairy-tale imp who spins straw into gold and tricks the miller's daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grimm fairy-tale character is a deceitful little goblin who bargains for a firstborn baby.

clue.text: Some hesitation in retrospectively entering painter's age

indicators.note: entering means these pieces go inside the painter's name

parts.note: William Etty was an English painter of nudes
er is a hesitant sound

indicators.note: retrospectively means looking back, so the small word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An art historian notes a moment of hesitation over an artist's era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'age' looks like the painter's period, but it is the definition. William Etty was a Victorian painter of nudes.
explanation.definitionFit: An age, informally, is a very long time, as is an endless span of time.

clue.text: A little hair of the dog consumed by X last of all

parts.note: X stands for a kiss at the end of a letter
a cur is a mongrel dog

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of all

explanation.surface: A hangover cure taken by someone at the very end of the night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hair of the dog' suggests a hangover drink, but 'A little hair' is the definition. X for a kiss comes from signing off letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A small curl of hair pressed flat on the forehead or cheek is a type of hairstyle.

clue.text: Striptease and other bawdy stuff, as naughty sequel to back massage

indicators.note: back means the word for massage is read in reverse

parts.note: to rub is to massage

indicators.note: naughty signals the letters of sequel misbehave into a new order

explanation.surface: A cheeky follow-up to a back rub leads to saucy entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back massage' reads as one phrase, but 'back' is the reversal signal on the massage word.
explanation.definitionFit: Variety entertainment featuring striptease and ribald comedy is called this, especially in America.

clue.text: Party held by cat is gatecrashed by fellow creature

indicators.note: held by means the party is placed inside the cat

parts.note: the Rex is a breed of cat, such as the Cornish Rex

indicators.note: gatecrashed by means the fellow intrudes into the party

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: A cat throws a party and an uninvited man barges in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cat' is not a feline synonym but a breed name, as in Cornish Rex.
explanation.definitionFit: A common wild animal of the dog family with a russet coat.

clue.text: Instrument not working for Italian singer

indicators.note: on means working, so not working removes the word on

parts.note: the bassoon is a woodwind instrument

explanation.surface: An orchestral player's instrument breaks, so a vocalist steps in.
explanation.definitionFit: Basso is the Italian term for a bass voice or a singer with one.

clue.text: Something of use after "black dog"

indicators.note: after places the useful thing behind the letter

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
an asset is something useful

explanation.surface: The phrase black dog, meaning depression, is followed by something useful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'black dog' looks like one quoted unit, but 'black' gives B and 'dog' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The basset hound is a short-legged breed of hunting hound.

clue.text: Port in Czech Republic initially allowing free passage for musician?

indicators.note: in places the port inside the country code

parts.note: CZ is the international code for the Czech Republic
Aden is a port in Yemen

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of allowing

explanation.surface: Someone at a Czech port is granted free movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free passage' sounds like travel rights but means an improvised-sounding solo section.
explanation.definitionFit: A virtuoso solo section in a concerto, often improvised, lets the performer play freely.

clue.text: Stuff for starters cooked with butter

indicators.note: for starters takes the opening letter of cooked

parts.note: a ram is a butter, an animal that butts

explanation.surface: A recipe direction for preparing a first course with butter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' looks like the dairy product, but means a thing that butts.
explanation.definitionFit: To stuff something is to pack or force it full, a synonym.

clue.text: Ready to join firm with established income earner

parts.note: the ready is slang for money, cash
Co is short for company, a firm

explanation.surface: Money is invested in a well-established, profitable company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' looks like an adjective, but is British slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A business or product that reliably generates profit is known by this metaphor.

clue.text: Cut and blow

definitions.meaning: to trim or snip with shears
a smack or cuff, as in a ... round the ear

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both trimming with scissors and a sharp smack.

clue.text: One to measure up

parts.note: a means one
a foot is a unit of length

explanation.surface: A single unit for measuring height.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' looks like a direction, but it means happening, as in 'what's up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something going on or in progress is up, as in mischief being afoot.

clue.text: Three-faced male doctor within hearing

indicators.note: within places the pieces inside the hearing

parts.note: a trial is a court hearing
he is a male pronoun

explanation.surface: A two-faced male doctor is outdone by a three-faced one in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A geometric solid angle formed by three planes meeting at a point has three faces.
